editorial:
Imagine being twelve years old and losing your voice because of some mean bullies. That is exactly what happens to Sunbo, who ends up swallowing a sea roach during a prank. Instead of just being sick, something strange happens: the creature settles inside his soul. For the next seven years, Sunbo cannot speak to anyone in the real world, but he has a secret best friend living inside him. You get to watch their weird but sweet bond grow as they share thoughts and feelings that no one else understands. It feels like a cozy, mysterious dream that makes you think about loneliness and friendship in a totally new way.

The acting is really natural, and the way the movie shows the mental link between the boy and the creature is super creative. While the middle part slows down a bit, the emotional payoff at the end makes it worth the wait. You should definitely check this out if you like stories that are a bit magical but still feel real. To get the best experience, try streaming it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video to see the beautiful colors. If you are a movie collector, adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection is a great call because the visuals are just that stunning.
endingExplained: At the end, Sunbo turns nineteen, and the sea roach must finally leave his body. This separation is painful but necessary for him to grow up. As the creature departs, Sunbo suddenly regains his ability to speak. He uses his first words to thank the creature for saving him from loneliness. He finally makes peace with his past bullies and starts living a normal life, carrying the lessons of their friendship forever.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves stories about unlikely friendships and magical realism.
